columns.description: First day of the calendar quarter the observation describes.
columns.name: period

columns.description: The OECD reference-area code, an ISO-3166 alpha-3 country code or an aggregate code such as EA, EU or OECD.
columns.name: reference_area_code

columns.description: The area name exactly as the OECD publishes it.
columns.name: reference_area_name

columns.description: Whether the area is an OECD member, a computed aggregate, or a non-member the OECD publishes alongside members.
columns.name: reference_area_kind

columns.description: Whether the row is for all people, men only or women only.
columns.name: sex

columns.description: Harmonised labour force participation rate as a percentage of the working-age population aged 15 or over in the same area and sex. Comparable with the French all-ages activity rate, not with the French 15-to-64 rate.
columns.name: participation_rate_pct

indicators.attribution: Source: OECD, Labour force participation rate. This is an adaptation of an original work by the OECD.
indicators.definition: OECD harmonised labour force participation rate for people aged 15 or over, seasonally adjusted, expressed as a percentage of the working-age population in the same subgroup. The matching French series is french-labour-market-quarterly.participation_rate_pct, the all-ages activity rate, which is the same 15-or-over basis; across the 94 shared quarters the two differ by at most 0.7 points after harmonisation. The French participation_rate_15_to_64_pct is a DIFFERENT basis, roughly 18 points higher, a gap that is a difference of denominator rather than of labour-market behaviour, so the two series do not measure the same quantity.
indicators.source: OECD, Labour force participation rate, dataflow DSD_LFS@DF_IALFS_LF_WAP_Q

model.description: One row per quarter, OECD reference area and sex, carrying the harmonised labour force participation rate for people aged 15 or over, seasonally adjusted, with each area classified as an OECD member, a computed aggregate or a non-member the OECD also publishes.
model.name: oecd_participation_comparison

questions.derivation: Select the five default reference areas with sex equal to all, and compare over time.
questions.question: Does a larger or smaller share of France's population take part in the labour market than in Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy and Spain?

questions.derivation: For each area and quarter, compare the men row with the women row. The gap is a difference between two published rates, not a published figure itself.
questions.question: Is the gap between men's and women's participation wider in France than elsewhere?

questions.derivation: Filter to rows whose reference_area_kind is member and select the areas the reader picked.
questions.question: How does France's participation rate compare with any other OECD economy the reader chooses?

temporal.grain: quarter by reference area and sex
temporal.meaning: Each period is the first day of the calendar quarter the observation describes. The grain is one row per period, reference_area_code and sex. Areas reach the publication edge at different speeds, so the latest quarter present differs by country.

validations.description: The compound key of period, reference_area_code and sex is unique.
validations.name: one-row-per-area-sex-and-quarter

validations.description: No published column is ever null.
validations.name: required-values

validations.description: Every area is a member, an aggregate or a non-member.
validations.name: area-kinds-are-known

validations.description: Every row is for all people, men or women.
validations.name: sexes-are-known

validations.description: Every area except Brazil, Croatia and the OECD aggregate carries all three sex breakdowns in every quarter it reports, so a participation gap can always be drawn for any of them.
validations.name: sex-split-is-complete-outside-known-gaps

validations.description: Every OECD member on the package's membership list appears, including Switzerland and New Zealand, which this quarterly dataflow carries although the monthly unemployment one does not.
validations.name: every-oecd-member-is-present

validations.description: Every aggregate the package classifies appears, except the G7, which this quarterly dataflow is known not to carry. Members and aggregates together are what guarantee whichever comparators a consumer chooses.
validations.name: every-declared-aggregate-is-present
